# HCodeBlock

> Escaped, copyable code or configuration text with optional wrapping and line numbers.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.5.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HCodeBlock` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-code-block>`.
- Constructor: `HearthCodeBlockElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Surfaces.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HCodeBlock.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Code is rendered as escaped plain text. language is a label, not a promise of syntax highlighting.
- Clipboard actions require browser clipboard access. Handle copy-error or let the visible error guide manual copying. Raw code, not rendered line numbers, is copied.

## Public API

code, language, title: string · wrap, lineNumbers, copyable: boolean

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    code: string;
    language?: string;
    title?: string;
    wrap?: boolean;
    lineNumbers?: boolean;
    copyable?: boolean;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ language: "text", copyable: true }
```

### Events

copied(), copy-error(message)

```ts
type Emits = {
    copied: [
    ];
    "copy-error": [
        message: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, header, code

Use `hearth-code-block::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HCodeBlock } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';
const command = 'docker compose up -d';
</script>

<template>
  <HCodeBlock :code="command" title="Start your service" language="sh" line-numbers />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-code-block');
Object.assign(element, {
  "code": "docker compose up -d",
  "title": "Start your service",
  "language": "sh",
  "lineNumbers": true
});

mount.append(element);
```
